title: A systematic survey of millimetre-wavelength flaring variability of young stellar objects in the Orion Nebula Cluster
question: What is the occurrence rate and nature of strong, short-term (minutes to days) millimeter-wavelength flaring variability in Young Stellar Objects (YSOs) in the Orion Nebula Cluster, and how do systematic time-sliced imaging effects and flares impact millimeter flux and disk mass measurements?

recipe.goal: Time-sliced and concatenated continuum imaging with spatial filtering
recipe.method: Image pipeline-calibrated visibilities in Stokes I (and Stokes Q for ORBS) using multi-frequency synthesis (mfs) in CASA TCLEAN with a uv-range cut (>138 klambda) to filter extended emission, creating a concatenated image, 8 epoch images (1.16 h), 24 sub-epoch images (20 min), 17 images (4 min), and 265 high-cadence images (8 s).
key_parameters: image size = 2048 x 2048 pixels, pixel size = 0.05 arcsec, pblim = 0.2
assumptions: Extended structures larger than ~1.5 arcsec are thermal dust/nebular emission that do not vary on timescales of minutes to days.

recipe.goal: Simulate ALMA observations to quantify systematic artificial variability
recipe.method: Generate 100 2D Gaussian constant artificial source models combined with 3 real background cutouts from the concatenated image (300 sky models), simulate visibilities across 7 hour angles (1 h each) using Simobserve, image with Simanalyze, extract fluxes with iterative IMFIT, and compute the variability factor (VF = max/min peak flux density).
key_parameters: Source FWHM = 0.1 to 0.9 arcsec; peak flux density = 5 to 100 mJy beam^-1
Hour angles = -5 h to +1 h (7 observations of 1 h each); pixel size = 0.05 arcsec; image size = 100 x 100 pixels
assumptions: Artificial sources have constant intrinsic flux density; measured flux variations arise from the changing synthesized beam interacting with source structure and complex background.

recipe.goal: Source detection, photometry, and multiwavelength catalog cross-matching
recipe.method: Visually inspect the concatenated continuum map and automatically search at positions of known X-ray (COUP), cm (VLA), and mm (CARMA, ALMA) sources; extract peak flux densities and deconvolved sizes using iterative Gaussian fitting (IMFIT) with a 5-sigma detection threshold; cross-match against X-ray, cm, mm, and optical/IR disk catalogs.
key_parameters: Detection threshold = 5 sigma; catalog cross-match search radius = 0.5 arcsec (extended to 1.0 arcsec for additional counterparts/disks)
assumptions: Distance to the ONC is ~400 pc.

recipe.goal: Light curve extraction, variability factor (VF) analysis, and physical flare characterization
recipe.method: Measure peak flux densities of the 133 catalog sources across the 1-h, 20-min, 4-min, and 8-s time-sliced images using IMFIT (adopting 3x local rms noise as upper limit when S/N < 5); compute VF = S_max / S_min; derive emitting region size upper limit from light travel time of the flare rise and estimate brightness temperature and radio luminosity.
key_parameters: Detection threshold = 5 sigma per time bin; non-detection upper limit = 3 sigma (local rms); systematic variability threshold VF = 2
assumptions: Light travel time during the ~4 min rise time sets the maximum radius of the flare emitting region (r < 0.5 au); dust mass is directly proportional to flux density at fixed dust temperature (M_dust proportional to S_nu).

score_reason: The ALMA project code, CASA version (5.4.1), calibrators, imaging parameters (Hogbom, Briggs robust=0.5, 2048x2048, 0.05 arcsec cell, pblim=0.2, uv cut >138 klambda), time-slicing intervals, and source catalog are all explicitly documented. rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA Band 3 continuum dataset (2017.1.01313.S) with a clear, well-specified time-sliced imaging and photometry recipe leading to sharp numeric results (the 10-minute, ~5.8 mJy beam^-1 flare in ORBS and 10x variability in Sources 86 and 87).
